title: Playing with Manuel Perez and the Onward band; decline of old bands and low pay
summary: Robertson played extra with Perez and the old bands, says school bands and the new music killed them off, and recalls working for a dollar a night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: We have a lot of later pictures of parades and all, just hoping to find some of those real old bands. I was going to ask about Manuel Perez and the Onward band. Oh yeah, old, yeah.

I, oh yeah, I play with old, Perez, Onward band. Years ago I went along with them, you know, play extra with them, you know. I play with all them old band actually. They come and get me. Mad drums sometimes, sometimes bassmen, all them old times. All those old time bands, they, they went out so, certainly, when this new stuff come in, old bands, look like they just went out. I tell you what started that, those school bands. See the people tried to pull me those school bands, you know. Yep. And Perez rather than the higher bands pay the money to get the school bands for less than nothing. Bands just went down. Men got scattered. Now I mean you could get them together. Now the people is calling for that type of back, and it's hard to get the men back. You take a lot of them and give it up. Not playing anymore. Not everything you can get out. They got the instruments, they got the instruments there man. Been laying up, they got instruments in there. When they opened the case, they looked at it. Look like it's been there a hundred years. Yeah, haven't touched it for you. Oh, I don't fool that no more. Ain't nothing in it no more. I don't even give it up. I couldn't get nothing out of it. People want something for nothing. I have seen myself playing music, honest and true, for a dollar a night. At them times they didn't call them cavalry, they called them tunks, hunky-tunk. Well I see myself, we had five or six men playing in the band, getting a dollar, a dollar, a dollar, a dollar a night, a piece. I believe you're right here in this city.
I've heard about that too. I played it, I played it.
